audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the chart contradicted its own why: win[0..2] read Quinn while whys[0..2] said 'even skill', win[4] read Quinn while whys[4] said 'even skill', and win[3] and win[5] read Skill while their whys said Quinn favoured.
audit.why: The mirror set rows 3 and 5 to Quinn and row 6 to Tryndamere; the packet gives Skill for rows 0, 1, 2 and 4, which is also what this page's own prose says. Two items in, Vault is one dash on 12/11/10/9/8s and crit plus Undying Rage closes the duel.
audit.corrected: Skill, Skill, Skill, Quinn, Skill, Quinn, Tryndamere with ratings 5,5,5,3,5,3,6, in matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The header read diff EVEN beside diffRating 8.5/10, a red tone and a 'Hard matchup' footer, and no cooldown appeared for any of her abilities.
audit.why: 49.87% over 395 games is an even lane, not an 8.5/10. Blinding Assault is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 1025 range, Vault 12/11/10/9/8s at 675, Heightened Senses 50/45/40/35/30s.
audit.corrected: Header aligned to EVEN 6/10; the three cooldowns written into the phases and spikes where they change a decision.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page framed Vault as the ability to track — focus.text, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns and the loading screen all say Vault — while Blinding Assault appeared only as a passing mention of 'her blind'.
audit.why: Tryndamere's entire damage output is auto-attacks. A blind from 1025 range on a 9-11s cooldown turns all of it off for its duration; Vault only repositions her. The blind is the ability that decides whether an all-in works. Vault also briefly interrupts on contact and lands her at her own maximum attack range, which is why baiting it first is the sequence.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] rewritten to put Blinding Assault first and Vault second, with both cooldowns; phases[2] and phases[3] carry the same order.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quinn is female; report[2], report[9], dontsFull[0].d, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late and report[12] used 'he', 'his' and 'him'.
audit.why: The tldr on the same page says 'She pokes + kites', so the page disagrees with itself on screen.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Quinn contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Neither of you commits at 1. Blinding Assault pokes from 1025 — take the CS behind minions and bank your health for later.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Quinn's Vault is down.
edits.after: Still even: Harrier marks give her a bonus first hit, so do not stand on the minion she has marked.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Quinn must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Spinning Slash is 650 and Vault answers it at 675 — she leaves at her own attack range, so bait Vault before you commit.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Vault's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Hers: Blinding Assault switches your autos off on 11-9s and Vault resets the trade, so give ground and farm toward your items.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Quinn's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds, but Behind Enemy Lines lets her leave and take the map instead — answer it by crashing waves, not by chasing her.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Vault's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker is your spike, but her first item kites it — commit only after Vault.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Quinn carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: crit plus Undying Rage ends any duel she cannot kite. Quinn carry threat 8.5/10 — force it in the side lane.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Vault and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track her blind and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 8.5/10, Quinn carry threat 8.5/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Quinn carry threat 8.5/10.

edits.before: His early — survive to your spikes. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.
edits.after: Her item spikes — survive them. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.

edits.before: That is Quinn's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: That is Quinn's favourite window — refuse it and half her win condition is gone.

edits.before: Commit on Vault's cooldown, on your level-6 spike, and on your Stridebreaker timing. Make him flinch first.
edits.after: Commit on Blinding Assault's cooldown, on your level-6 spike, and on your Stridebreaker timing. Make her flinch.

edits.before: If Quinn gets a kill, stop forcing and respect Vault. Two kills: farm safe and call for jungle cover. If he snowballs, play for picks with your team — not solo redemption.
edits.after: If Quinn gets a kill, stop forcing and respect Vault. Two kills: farm safe and call for jungle cover. If she snowballs, play for picks with your team — not solo redemption.

edits.before: Two-plus items favours Quinn — ranged DPS plus roam mobility let her sidestep your all-ins and pressure the map.
edits.after: Two-plus items favours you — crit plus Undying Rage ends any duel one 8s Vault cannot kite away from.

edits.before: Your all-in threat exists but Quinn's Blinded Vault (E) dashes back off you and her Harrier (passive) procs chunk you every few autos, so trades stay roughly even unless she wastes E.
edits.after: Blinding Assault (Q) is the problem, not Vault: it blinds from 1025 range on 11-9s and your damage is all auto-attacks, so commit only once it is spent. Vault then dashes her back out on 12-8s.

edits.before: You get R Undying Rage to survive her burst, but Quinn's ultimate Behind Enemy Lines (R) lets her roam and snowball map pressure you can't answer while you shove.
edits.after: Undying Rage survives her burst, but Behind Enemy Lines lets her roam and build a lead you cannot answer while you shove — it is a channel, so any CC from your team cancels it.

edits.before: You want to be split-pushing and forcing 1v1s, but Quinn's mobility and repeated E knockback make her one of the cleaner kiters against your melee crit windows.
edits.after: Split-push and force 1v1s: Vault is one dash on 12/11/10/9/8s, so bait it out first. Mocking Shout only slows her while her back is turned, so make her run rather than reposition.

edits.before: On items and beyond Quinn is favoured — her ranged DPS, Vault knockback, and roam pressure kite your crit all-ins, so you must win by split-pushing rather than dueling her head-on.
edits.after: First item is hers, but by two items you turn it — Vault is a single dash on 12-8s, and once it is spent your crit plus Undying Rage closes the duel. Split-push and make her answer you.
